clue.text: Text like this many deem tabu

definitions.meaning: every word of this clue (text, like, this, many, deem, tabu) has exactly four letters, so the clue is itself an example
swear words are the classic taboo vocabulary, crude terms that many people consider unsayable

explanation.surface: A remark that some piece of writing contains words many people would consider off-limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters of each clue word: all six have four, so the clue demonstrates its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude swear words are traditionally called this because so many of the commonest ones are short, taboo terms of four letters.

clue.text: Lives created in self-reliant way

parts.note: lives here are written life stories, and self-reliant means produced by the subject themselves rather than by another writer

explanation.surface: Seems to describe people who live independently, making their own way in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like a verb or the plural of life lived; it is the noun for written life stories. 'Self-reliant' hints at the Greek prefix for self.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts of a person's life written by that same person are memoirs of this kind, life stories produced by their own subject.

clue.text: Numbers of solutions including old slang turned up in print

indicators.note: including means the pair of values holds the next part between them

parts.note: pH is the number measuring the acidity of a chemical solution; plural numbers gives two of them, PH and PH

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: argot is the slang or jargon of a particular group

explanation.surface: Appears to be about how often answers to puzzles contain dated slang that has surfaced in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solutions' suggests crossword answers but means chemical liquids, whose acidity is given as a pH value. 'Turned up' suits a down clue, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A print is a copy made photographically on paper, so the two words name the same picture.

clue.text: Self-reference in book published without purpose

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the publishing word goes around the next part

parts.note: ran, as in a newspaper ran the story, means published
an end is an aim or purpose, as in to that end

explanation.surface: Sounds like a complaint about a book that came out with no clear point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the setter's own pseudonym, hence 'Self-reference': in this puzzle the setter names themself.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's pseudonym is the name the puzzle's compiler uses, so writing it in the grid refers to its own creator.

clue.text: A head among teachers

definitions.note: as in tickets cost five pounds a head, meaning per person

indicators.note: among says the letters are found inside the word teachers

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a headteacher working among the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' reads as a school head, but it is the phrase for per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Priced 'a head' means per person, the same as saying for every individual one.

clue.text: Completely normal way to enter answer like this

definitions.meaning: the phrase means thoroughly or in every part, as in cleaned the house fully

definitions.text: normal way to enter answer like this
definitions.meaning: a down answer such as this one is written into the grid starting at the highest square and ending at the lowest

explanation.surface: Seems to be an instruction about how solvers should fill in their answers.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so its own answer is entered in exactly the way the phrase describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over something in its entirety, head to foot, is an idiom for doing it completely.

clue.text: Requires no explanation from small summits, since left is represented

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
peaks are mountain tops or summits
for can mean since or because, as in 'for he was tired'

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to say that small summits need no explanation because the political left is represented there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges LEFT IS into ITSELF; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is self-evident is idiomatically said to need no further comment or justification from anyone.

clue.text: One's not self-sufficient creating work that's bound to be finished

definitions.text: One's not self-sufficient creating work that's bound to be finished

parts.words: One's not self-sufficient creating work that's bound to be finished
parts.note: a work that's bound is a book; someone who needs a partner to write one is not self-sufficient as a writer

explanation.surface: Sounds like a dependent person doing a job that is certain to be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it means a book with a binding; 'finished' is the completed book.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who shares the writing of a book with a partner does not produce it alone, hence not self-sufficient.

clue.text: Page in article, very dry and short

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in puts the page letter inside the dry-wine word

parts.note: brut describes the driest champagnes and sparkling wines

explanation.surface: A page of some article is described as very dry and brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very dry' is a wine label term, BRUT, rather than a comment on dull writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short or curt manner is brusque, sudden and lacking in politeness, which is this adjective's sense.

clue.text: Fish around end of jetty as test

indicators.note: around means the fish word encloses the next letter

parts.note: a trout is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word jetty

explanation.surface: An angler tries for fish around the end of a jetty to test the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run or audition used to evaluate something is a test of its quality before it is adopted.

clue.text: He repeatedly gets involved with main book in old collection

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together with those of main
repeatedly means the word He is written twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting involved with the main book in an old collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved with' scrambles HEHE and MAIN together. The 'old collection' is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the historical books of the Old Testament, the older collection of biblical scripture.

clue.text: Spirit originally from Persia, mostly

indicators.note: from means that letter is taken away out of what remains of Persia
mostly means all of the word Persia except its final letter
originally means the first letter of the word Spirit

explanation.surface: A spirit whose origins lie chiefly in Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: in Persian mythology this is a fairy-like spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian folklore this is a beautiful supernatural being, a fairy or sprite, so a spirit originating in Persia.

clue.text: Detention facility not recommended for stoners

definitions.meaning: British military slang for an army prison, from the glass-roofed one at Aldershot
the proverb says those who live in a house made of panes should not throw stones

explanation.surface: Seems to advise that a certain prison is unsuitable for people who take drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoners' suggests cannabis users; it means people throwing stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse is fragile, so the proverb warns its residents against throwing stones; separately it is military slang for a detention barracks.

clue.text: Something said by self-described birdwatcher?

parts.note: someone who mangles words by swapping their initial sounds might call themself a word botcher, which comes out as bird watcher

explanation.surface: Asks what a person who calls themself a keen birder might say.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the initial sounds of 'word botcher', someone who mangles words, and it becomes 'bird watcher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a transposition of initial sounds, named after the Oxford don William Spooner, is exactly what turns word botcher into birdwatcher.

clue.text: Staying out — it's hellishly dark

indicators.note: out here means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Remarks that staying outdoors is dreadfully dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Styx, the river of the classical underworld, the word means gloomy and dark as Hades.

clue.text: Bridge as card game

definitions.meaning: a floating structure of boats or floats supporting a roadway across water
the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack

explanation.surface: Seems to say bridge is a card game, which it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game, but here it is a floating crossing; the card game is the other definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating bridge resting on boats has this name, and so does the British version of blackjack, twenty-one.

clue.text: A way to travel on horseback

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Simply describes riding as a means of getting around on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with one leg on each side, as a rider does on a horse, is the posture this word describes.

clue.text: Is inspiring brain excited with these

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of these two words are mixed

explanation.surface: Something is stimulating, getting the brain excited with these ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' reads as stimulating, but it is used in its literal sense of drawing in air.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire literally means to inhale, drawing air into the lungs, so 'is inspiring' is the present tense of that.

clue.text: Edge attached to side of boater?

definitions.text: Edge attached to side of boater?

indicators.note: attached to means the edge word is fixed onto that letter
side of means the letter at one side, the start, of the word boater

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Describes the edge sticking out from the side of a straw boater hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat; the whole clue also describes the projecting edge around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The projecting edge that runs around a hat is this word, and a boater's is flat and stiff.

clue.text: Person exploring below porthole, moving right

indicators.note: moving means that letter is shifted to another place in the word porthole

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a sailor below decks peering out of a porthole and moving right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below' seems to place the person under a porthole on a ship; it means underground, in caves.
explanation.definitionFit: A caver who explores underground cave systems and shafts is someone exploring below the surface.

clue.text: Stand test of time, like this clue

definitions.meaning: to endure or keep going for a long time
this is the final clue in the list, coming after all the others

explanation.surface: Hopes a clue will endure and be remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the final clue in the puzzle, so it describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to keep going over time, and the final item in a series is the one at the end.

clue.text: Setter's anagram subject to further examination

indicators.note: the word anagram itself openly says the letters of setter are to be rearranged

parts.note: the setter is the compiler of the crossword; the possessive says the anagram belongs to this word

explanation.surface: The setter's own anagram is put through more scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's anagram' means an anagram of the word setter, not one the setter wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something a second time, putting it through checks again, is a verb of the same sense.

clue.text: Producers of serpentine dreads?

indicators.note: serpentine means winding or twisting, so the letters of dreads are twisted round

explanation.surface: Asks what causes people's fear of snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The vipers in question produce snake fears; equally, an anagram 'serpentine' twists DREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: These venomous snakes are Britain's only native vipers, so they cause the fear people have of snakes.

clue.text: Robs special facility, splitting diamonds and paintings

indicators.note: splitting means it comes between the next two parts

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
oils are paintings done in oil paint
ESP, extrasensory perception, is a supposed special mental power

explanation.surface: Thieves raid a special facility that separates jewels from art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special facility' sounds like a building but means a sixth sense, ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or rob a place by force is to pillage it, the verb's original sense.
